newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - November 25.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Monday.
- Irish government spending plans agreed for next year will allow the Minister for Finance, Ruairi Quinn, to afford close to 250 million Irish pounds in tax cuts in the January Budget.
- Differences are still to be bridged by the British and Irish governments despite a weekend of intensive communications to try and bring about a new ceasefire by the Irish Republican Army.
- The Irish government did not tell the judiciary it was about to announce the establishment of a board to run the courts.
- European Union finance ministers reached a compromise late on Sunday to allow the Italian lira re-enter the exchange rate mechanism of the European Monetary System.
- The Irish government is considering a radical new approach to funding local authorities.
- There was conflicting signals on Sunday about the prospects of a new IRA ceasefire.
- Two Irish trade associations on Sunday called for concerted action to tackle the growing problem of business crime which, they say, is threatening the viability of many small businesses.

- British finance minister Kenneth Clarke, seeking to defuse a growing row over Europe in his badly divided Conservative Party, on Sunday pledged to make a statement to the UK parliament over monetary union.
